profile.bio: Most of my working life has gone into making operational data usable. I ran asset management for a solar portfolio above $100M for four years: yield models that passed bank audits, mobile field capture, and telemetry reconciliation when sensors went missing. Since 2023 I have run thirteen NixOS hosts from one flake, with an SSH certificate authority and encrypted secrets per host. The free hours go to CISA's KEV catalogue, building tools that turn the exploited list into a patch order a team can work through.

focus.title: Reproducible fleets
focus.body: Thirteen machines, one repository. Rebuilding a host, auditing it or handing it to someone else takes the commit, not a folder of install notes.

focus.title: Go services with bounded work
focus.body: One binary per service, serving HTML, JSON and a terminal UI. Small enough to read in an afternoon, and state is a log of what happened rather than a row someone edited.

focus.title: Vulnerability data that ends in action
focus.body: CISA's exploited list as a time series and as clusters a team can finish this week. The output is a patch order, not another dashboard.

work.title: Multi-host NixOS fleet
work.description: I moved thirteen machines off per-host install notes and onto one repository. Rebuilding, auditing or handing over a host is now the commit plus one command; secrets are encrypted per host and certificates rotate on a schedule.

work.title: bountystash: deterministic work engine
work.description: A request arrives as prose and has drifted by the time the work is done. I built a Go service that records it as an immutable document, so a job's state replays a month later and two people can agree on what was asked. One binary serves HTML, JSON and a terminal UI.

work.title: fibtransponder
work.description: I set out to build a stream detector and wrote the benchmark first. The measurement killed the first design, so what ships is the smaller claim: a state machine whose work per step stays bounded, with the corpus that falsified the rest in the repository.

work.title: Energy telemetry and valuation
work.description: Four years running the numbers behind a solar portfolio above $100M: yield and valuation models that satisfied bank auditors, mobile capture for field technicians, and a reconciliation step that turned a dead sensor into a known error instead of a good month.

work.title: Smart Energy 360
work.description: Built and ran a project pipeline above $100M for commercial clients moving to cleaner electricity, with the sustainability strategy and the risk advice that went with it.

work.title: Fraunhofer ISE
work.description: Measured heliostat imperfections with interferometry: C++ for the instrument, Python for analysis and 3D geometry.

work.title: Halliburton
work.description: Two frac crews in the Bakken shale: chemicals and equipment faults fixed on site, twelve-hour shifts, and the safety training for the crew.

lab.title: The KEV lab
lab.body: Two public tools read CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue. kev-time plots exploitation over time, so a trend shows up before a report does. kelly-svg groups entries into clusters a team can work through, so patch order follows effort and exposure. Both are static SVG and plain HTML, readable on a phone during an incident. concept.bountystash.com puts the same data into a programme: a sample queue grouped by effort.

hire.title: What I am looking for
hire.body: A senior or lead role where infrastructure and security meet: platform engineering, site reliability, or vulnerability operations. Remote from a CET base, or on site in Freiburg and the Upper Rhine.
